raw_response:
I am already old, 66 this year, so I do not want to spread my hands too wide. My land is only 5 mu, and there are just 2 people in the house, so I will still keep cotton as the main crop and leave a smaller piece for mungbean. Cotton is slower and takes more picking, but in our place I know how to manage it, and with the well I am not so afraid of spring dryness. Mungbean I keep mainly because it needs less fertilizer, the cash pressure is lighter, and if cotton price or weather is not good, at least I still have another crop.

I finished middle school, so I do listen a bit to the township advice, but in the end I still farm by what I have seen on my own field. Last year if I fed cotton too little, the plants stayed weak and boll setting was poor, so this year I will not cut fertilizer too much. But I also cannot spend heavily, so I will use a moderate rate, mostly base fertilizer plus one topdressing. For mungbean I will keep inputs light, because this crop can stand poorer land better. Water costs money from the well, so I will not irrigate many times unless the field is really dry. For pesticides, I will not spray by habit only; for cotton I will watch aphids and bollworm, and for mungbean I mainly watch leaf-eating insects and weeds.
